subject: Inference deployment: HIPAA / SOC2 tradeoffs and proposed sprint for BAA/Hosted vs Dedicated
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brighthealthai.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@brighthealthai.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call: deployment options (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) + next steps for HIPAA/BAA evidence

Hi Lena & Samir —

Great to meet earlier. Short recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned on compliance-driven deployment options. High-level takeaway from our call: BrightHealth wants production-ready inference with patient PHI allowed under a BAA, predictable SLAs, and the option to avoid public multi-tenant inference for specific workloads. That maps to three candidate paths:

- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted): fastest to go-live; we offer BAA + data routing controls, but some customers with strict audit requirements prefer Dedicated or Private because of isolation and deeper network controls.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in our cloud for your account; provides tenant isolation, predictable throughput, and support for stricter access controls.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-managed network and optional on-prem package for environments that require air-gapped operation or customer KMS/HSM.

Per our conversation, your priorities in order: 1) BAA in place, 2) SOC2 evidence and architecture diagrams for procurement, 3) clear audit timeline (internal security review + vendor risk assessment) and 4) an SLA commitment for P95 latency on critical endpoints.

Next steps I propose (short timeline so procurement can start):
1) I attach a concise Redwood_Security_Pack.pdf with SOC2 summary, network diagram templates, and our standard BAA — please treat the BAA draft as a starting point.
2) Dev (cc'd) will produce a one-page Dedicated vs Hosted feature matrix tailored to your PHI flows (ETA: 48 hours).
3) Mark (cc'd) from Infra Solutions will coordinate a short technical Q&A (30–45m) to validate your audit team's checklist items and confirm evidence formats for SOC2 artifacts (ETA: calendar invite by EOD tom).
4) You confirm whether you need on-prem (air-gapped) evaluation now or we can scope it later. If on-prem is required we will add a short discovery sprint to size hardware and network requirements.

Would you like us to prioritize a Dedicated configuration (we can provision a staging pool for a POC) or try to accelerate Hosted + BAA in parallel while we validate audit items?

Thanks again — I’ll jump on any follow-ups and keep things tight on timelines.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Pack.pdf, SOC2_Type2_summary.txt

Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment options (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) + next steps for HIPAA/BAA evidence

Thanks Ava — useful recap. A few clarifying Qs from our security team after reviewing the pack:

1) SOC2 artifacts: can you provide the latest Type II period and a point of contact for the auditor should our procurement need direct verification?
2) Data residency: our legal team wants confirmation that PHI processed under Hosted will not be replicated outside the US unless explicitly requested. Is that standard?
3) Audit logs: we need at least 90 days of immutable audit logs for any admin/console access — do you support that on Hosted or is that only possible on Dedicated/Private?
4) BAA edits: we reviewed the draft — a couple of legal comments re: liability cap and subprocessors (we'll share marked changes).

We prefer to avoid immediate on-prem unless necessary, but Dedicated looks appealing if the audit log and residency controls are available. Please route the SOC2 contact and confirm residency + audit log durability. Also include estimated cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted in a one-pager.

—Samir

Samir —

Thanks for the clear questions. Answers inline below and quick notes on next deliverables.

1) SOC2 artifacts: our latest SOC2 Type II period covers 2026-09 through 2027-03. Auditor contact: Crowne Audit LLP, audit@crowneaudit.com (we'll provide a letter of attestation and an auditor POC).

2) Data residency: Hosted accounts can be restricted to US-only regions; we guarantee no cross-border replication without customer opt-in. I'll include region routing details in the Dedicated vs Hosted matrix.

3) Audit logs: We provide 90-day retained audit logs by default for admin events on Hosted (immutable export available). For Dedicated we can offer extended retention (customizable up to 2 years) and access to raw log exports for your SIEM. Private/on-prem supports any retention you manage.

4) BAA edits: perfect — please share the marked changes and I'll loop Legal. We typically accept reasonable edits on liability thresholds for enterprise contracts.

Deliverables we will ship by Thu EOD:
- Dedicated-vs-Hosted-matrix.pdf (Dev) — 48 hours
- Cost delta one-pager (Ava) — estimate for Dedicated reservation sizes aligned to your projected QPS
- Schedule invite for technical Q&A with Mark (solutions) — targeting Fri morning your time

Markus will scope the audit-item evidence format (SOC2 artifacts list, KMS/HSM options for Private) and then we can confirm what goes into the procurement packet.

If you want to move faster on Hosted + BAA (so you can start sending test PHI), we'll prioritize legal and region controls to get you baseline protected ASAP while the Dedicated sizing runs in parallel.

One small ask: could you share the vendor risk assessment template your procurement uses? It speeds the evidence mapping.

Thanks —
Ava

Hi Samir / Lena —

Following Ava's notes, quick technical plan and ask from Infra Solutions:

Summary: Hosted with BAA is the fastest path. Dedicated is recommended if you want isolation + longer log retention + dedicated GPUs for predictable latency. Private (VPC/on-prem) only if procurement requires customer-managed keys or physical air-gapping.

Technical checklist we can provide in the Q&A (we'll prepare the artifacts in advance):
- SOC2 attestation letter + inventory of controls (pdf)
- Network diagram (redacted) showing region routing and ingress/egress controls
- Audit log export sample and retention policy details
- KMS/HSM integration patterns (for Dedicated + Private) and key custody options
- SLA addendum template for P95 latency and availability targets

Proposed sprint to close procurement (4 working days):
Day 1: Deliver Dedicated vs Hosted matrix + cost delta one-pager (Dev)
Day 2: Provide SOC2 letter, network diagram, and sample audit logs (Markus)
Day 3: Legal exchange on BAA redlines (Ava + Legal)
Day 4: Joint technical Q&A and procurement packet handoff; if Dedicated selected, start provisioning staging pool.

Request from BrightHealth: please send vendor risk assessment template and any required evidence format (PDF checklist preferred). Also confirm whether you want us to include a BAA that references a specific SLA or leave SLA separately in the procurement addendum.

Looking forward to the Q&A — I'll send a calendar invite for Fri 08/06 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET unless you suggest otherwise.
